items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Lieutenant, Fire Lieutenant, they named Lieutenant Lyons, too. I said, all right, Robson, you want to play trombone? I said, yes, sir.

ctx.x: I took a chance, man, walk up there.

Lieutenant, Fire Lieutenant, they named Lieutenant Lyons, too. I said, all right, Robson, you want to play trombone? I said, yes, sir. I said, all right. I said, well, give me a brand new chord on trombone. So I just took it and put it together, you know. But I could pull it up, understand? Well, every day, so after, they had a fella who was working with the band, but it was three or four weeks, and he couldn't even pull his horn up. items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: And so, Lieutenant Lion said, this is my band, I can't, little, little Lion said, this is my band, I'll bring watch out. And so the father said, Lieutenant Lion's come on, boy, he's a good lieutenant too, man. Because he had done dressed me up

ctx.x: Yeah. on his hands, came on with the band, was a good position. And William Foster, you know, all the people, you know. And William Foster said, Bob, you called me Bob, he said, he said, let's come and get the band with us, with the lines. And they brought all them boys, put them on nice, put them shoes, rustling shoes, tanned shoes, they brought them heavy shoes, with them nails on. William said, I can help you. And he said, yeah, Bob. And so they talked to Lieutenant Lyons, I said, Lord have mercy that morning.…
